subject.title: [Feature]: On-device LLM option for iOS Talk Mode

question: Should iOS Talk Mode become a supported on-device LLM product surface, and if so, what minimum backend, model-distribution, fallback, and device-support contract should OpenClaw own?
rationale: The request creates new capability and configuration surfaces with platform, storage, privacy, and provider-routing consequences; source-level repair judgment cannot choose the permanent product contract safely.

options.title: Sponsor a phased native design
options.body: Approve a narrowly scoped first phase with an owner-defined supported backend and explicit device, model, fallback, and privacy contracts before implementation begins.

options.title: Keep gateway-backed Talk only
options.body: Decline a built-in local-model route for now and retain the current Talk architecture while documenting the product boundary.

options.title: Route to an extension seam first
options.body: Prioritize a generic iOS inference/provider seam only if maintainers want third-party local-model implementations without committing to a bundled backend.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a phased native design
recommendation.body: Approve a narrowly scoped first phase with an owner-defined supported backend and explicit device, model, fallback, and privacy contracts before implementation begins.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the only evidence-backed adjacent iOS Talk contributor in the supplied related-item history; direct ownership remains unconfirmed.
